cards.name: Invert
cards.summary: Flips the polarity (phase) of the clip's audio by 180 degrees. On its own it sounds identical; it only matters when the clip is mixed with a second mic or another copy of the same sound.
use_for: Fix a thin, hollow interview mix when one of two mics on the same take (lav + boom) was recorded with reversed polarity: invert that mic's clip
Null-test two renders or two versions of a mix: invert one copy on a second track, whatever you still hear is the difference
avoid: Expecting an audible change on a single solo track: nothing changes
It flips all channels; it cannot invert just the left or right side
Cancelling music or bleed with an inverted copy only works when both copies are identical and sample-aligned; a camera mic and a clean file never null
Lav/boom comb filtering caused by distance (time offset) is not fixed by Invert: nudge the clips into sync instead
cards.scripting: No settable parameters. The only harvested row is an unnamed boolean, very likely the component's Bypass switch: leave it false. Apply by name with QE addAudioEffect; presence = on. To prove it works, put a duplicate of the clip on a second track with Invert on one copy: the pair should cancel to near-silence. Effects-panel folder is a best guess. Measured on a split stereo pair: both channels come out with inverted polarity (correlation -1 with the dry input) at unchanged level.

measured.how: Premiere 26 render, 3 s test signal per setting, analysed with ffmpeg (live wave 3, 2026-10-14)

cards.name: Lowpass
cards.summary: Removes frequencies above the Cutoff and lets the lows through, so sound becomes muffled and distant. Keyframing the Cutoff gives the classic muffled-to-full sweep.
use_for: Muffle music while a character goes underwater, faints or drifts into a flashback
Make music sound like it plays in another room before a reveal or door-open
Sweep music from muffled to full at a trailer or reel beat drop
Gently tame hiss on a noisy archival clip
avoid: Using it on VO: speech loses clarity fast once the cutoff drops into the presence range
A static, extreme cutoff on a whole music track sounds broken rather than stylised

params.name: Cutoff
params.does: Frequency above which sound is removed; normalized 0..1, higher = brighter (more highs kept). Measured on pink noise: -3 dB at 66 Hz / 1.2 kHz / 4.8 kHz / 11.3 kHz for 0.05 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75, close to Hz = 18 000 x v^1.9 (within about 12 %).
params.typical: default 0.25 (-3 dB at 1.2 kHz, measured); telephone top 3.4 kHz = 0.42; 500 Hz muffle = 0.16; 1 for nearly open

cards.scripting: Cutoff is exposed normalized 0..1 (default 0.25). The API does not report Hz; measured -3 dB points follow Hz = 18 000 x v^1.9 (0.05 = 66 Hz, 0.5 = 4.8 kHz). The unnamed boolean row is very likely Bypass: leave false. For an 'other room' look, pair a fixed low Cutoff with -6 to -10 dB on Volume. Recipe sweeps 0.05 -> 1 over 1.5 s from clip start; 0.05 is only 66 Hz (measured), so the sweep starts near-silent: start it at 0.15 (about 500 Hz) for a muffled start.

measured.how: Premiere 26 render, 3 s test signal per setting, analysed with ffmpeg (live wave 3, 2026-10-14)

cards.name: Mute
cards.summary: Silences the clip's audio, either all channels at once or individual channels, and can be keyframed to silence just a section.
use_for: Silence a dead or noisy channel inside a multichannel camera clip (e.g. 4-channel XLR recording) while keeping the others; on a stereo pair use Fill Left with Right / Fill Right with Left instead so the good mic plays in both ears
Hard-silence a profanity or a name that must be dropped from a news bite (keyframed)
Silence a clip's audio temporarily while keeping it on the timeline for reference
avoid: Keyframed mute is a hard on/off and can click; use Volume keyframes with short ramps for smooth dips
To drop a clip's sound entirely, disabling or deleting the audio clip is cleaner

params.name: Mute All
params.does: Silences every channel (0 = sound on, 1 = muted). Measured: 1 silences the clip (-129 dB), 0 leaves it unchanged.

params.name: Mute 1
params.does: Silences channel 1 only (0 = on, 1 = muted)
params.typical: 1 to drop a bad first channel

cards.scripting: Harvested on a mono clip, so only 'Mute All' and 'Mute 1' are named; the 31 unnamed numeric rows after them are the slots for channels 2-32 (Premiere's 32-channel maximum; on multichannel clips they are expected to appear as Mute 2, Mute 3...; unverified). Values are normalized 0..1 toggles: set 1 to mute, 0 to unmute. The first unnamed boolean is very likely Bypass. Keyframes are expected to act as hold on/off toggles (unverified: if a scripted ramp 0->1 fades instead, set hold interpolation). Effects-panel folder is a best guess; After Effects has no mute effect (use the layer audio switch or Audio Levels).

measured.how: Premiere 26 render, 3 s test signal per setting, analysed with ffmpeg (live wave 3, 2026-10-14)

cards.name: Simple Parametric EQ
cards.summary: A single-band bell EQ: boosts or cuts a band of frequencies around Center, with Q setting how narrow the band is.
use_for: Cut boxy or muddy room tone (around 200-400 Hz) on an interview
Add a small presence lift (around 3-5 kHz) so VO cuts through music
Carve a dip in a music bed where the narration sits
Quick one-band fix when the full Parametric Equalizer is overkill
avoid: Big boosts with a narrow Q ring and sound harsh
Stacking several copies for multi-band work: use Parametric Equalizer instead

params.name: Center
params.does: Centre frequency of the band; normalized 0..1 (default 0.25), measured about 24 000 x v^2 Hz. Measured: the band centre is about 24 000 x v^2 Hz (0.1 = 250 Hz, 0.25 = 1.6 kHz, 0.5 = 6.3 kHz, 0.75 = 12.7 kHz, third-octave readings): v = sqrt(Hz / 24 000).

measured.figure: band of the largest boost (Hz, third-octave resolution)

params.name: Q
params.does: Bandwidth: higher = narrower band
params.typical: 0.3-0.5 for broad musical moves; higher for surgical cuts

params.name: Boost
params.does: Gain at the centre; 0.5 = 0 dB (flat), below cuts, above boosts. Measured on pink noise at Center 0.25: 0.75 = +12.0 dB, 1 = +23.8 dB, so about 48 dB per unit around 0.5 (a +/-24 dB span); cuts read only as a notch.
params.typical: 0.46-0.48 for a 1-2 dB cut, 0.52-0.54 for a 1-2 dB lift

cards.scripting: Match name keeps Adobe's spelling 'Internal Parameteric EQ' (sic). All three controls are normalized 0..1 and Boost 0.5 is flat. The API reports no Hz or dB, but both are measured: Center about 24 000 x v^2 Hz, Boost about +/-24 dB. The unnamed boolean is very likely Bypass. Prefer 'Parametric Equalizer' for multi-band VO chains.

measured.how: Premiere 26 render, 3 s test signal per setting, analysed with ffmpeg (live wave 3, 2026-10-14)

cards.name: Swap Channels
cards.summary: Swaps the left and right channels of a stereo clip, so what was on the left plays on the right and vice versa.
use_for: Match channel order across cameras when one camera had its mic inputs reversed (lav on CH2 instead of CH1)
Keep on-screen sound positions matching after a shot was mirrored horizontally
Correct a stereo music or ambience file with reversed channels
avoid: Mono clips: there is nothing to swap and the effect does not attach
cards.scripting: Stereo clips only; no parameters of its own: it exchanges the left and right channels (measured: each output matches the opposite input) on a split stereo pair (live wave 3). The mono harvest could not attach it and read the clip Volume row; the batch now holds the stereo dump (match 'Internal Audio Swap Channels'). Apply it by name with QE addAudioEffect to a stereo clip and check the last component's displayName.

measured.how: Premiere 26 render, 3 s test signal per setting, analysed with ffmpeg (live wave 3, 2026-10-14)

cards.name: Fill Left with Right
cards.summary: Copies the right channel into the left and discards the original left, so both speakers play the right channel.
use_for: Interview where the good lav is only on the right channel: make it play in both ears
Remove a dead, noisy or camera-mic left channel from a field recording
Turn a one-sided dual-mono camera track into centred speech
avoid: It throws away the left channel: listen first, the left may be the better mic
Mono clips: no effect (it does not attach)
cards.scripting: Stereo clips only; no parameters of its own: it copies the right channel into the left, so both play the right side (measured) on a split stereo pair (live wave 3). The mono harvest could not attach it and read the clip Volume row; the batch now holds the stereo dump (match 'Internal Audio Fill Left'). Apply it by name with QE addAudioEffect to a stereo clip and check the last component's displayName.

measured.how: Premiere 26 render, 3 s test signal per setting, analysed with ffmpeg (live wave 3, 2026-10-14)

cards.name: Fill Right with Left
cards.summary: Copies the left channel into the right and discards the original right, so both speakers play the left channel.
use_for: Interview where the good mic is only on the left channel (common with camera XLR input 1): play it in both ears
Remove a dead or noisy right channel from a camera recording
Centre a dual-mono VO recorded into one input
avoid: It throws away the right channel: check it is not the better mic first
Mono clips: no effect (it does not attach)
cards.scripting: Stereo clips only; no parameters of its own: it copies the left channel into the right, so both play the left side (measured) on a split stereo pair (live wave 3). The mono harvest could not attach it and read the clip Volume row; the batch now holds the stereo dump (match 'Internal Audio Fill Right'). Apply it by name with QE addAudioEffect to a stereo clip and check the last component's displayName.

cards.name: Treble
cards.summary: High-shelf EQ with one Boost control that raises or lowers the high frequencies (roughly 4 kHz and up).
use_for: Add a little air and clarity to a dull lav VO
Cut tape hiss or a harsh top end on old archival audio (phone/WhatsApp audio has little above 4 kHz, so Treble barely changes it)
Darken a music bed slightly so narration sits on top
avoid: Boosting a noisy recording lifts hiss along with the voice
Big boosts on VO make S sounds harsh; add DeEsser if you must

params.name: Boost
params.does: High-shelf gain; 0.5 = 0 dB (flat), lower cuts, higher boosts. Measured at 10 kHz on pink noise: 0 = -15.5 dB, 0.25 = -8.6, 0.75 = +11.1, 1 = +23.9 dB; a full cut also takes about 7 dB off 1 kHz.
params.typical: VO: 0.52-0.58 for a slight lift; music bed under VO 0.40-0.45 (measured: -15.5 dB at 0, +23.9 dB at 1 at 10 kHz)

cards.scripting: Boost is normalized 0..1 with 0.5 = flat; the API reports no dB, but the span is measured (see Boost). The unnamed boolean is very likely Bypass. Keep moves small; for anything more precise use Parametric Equalizer.

measured.how: Premiere 26 render, 3 s test signal per setting, analysed with ffmpeg (live wave 3, 2026-10-14)

cards.name: Volume
cards.summary: Stackable gain effect that raises or lowers loudness and can be keyframed for fades and ducking. Same control as the fixed Volume every clip already has, but placed wherever you want in the effect chain.
use_for: Duck music under VO with keyframes (about -10 to -18 dB)
Fade SFX and music in and out
Add a gain stage after an EQ or compressor in the chain
Balance clip levels before final loudness normalisation
avoid: Pushing towards the scripted +15 dB maximum (the Effect Controls slider itself stops at +6 dB) on quiet VO also raises noise; use Audio Gain or Amplify first
Level 0 is silence (-infinity dB), not 0 dB

params.name: Level
params.does: Gain as normalized linear amplitude: value = 10^((dB - 15) / 20), so 0.17783 = 0 dB, 1.0 = +15 dB, 0 = silence. Measured on a tone: 0.0562 = -10.0 dB, 0.1778 = 0, 0.3162 = +5.0, 1 = +15.0 dB: the formula confirmed.

cards.scripting: Match 'Internal Volume'. Level uses Premiere's audio-level normalization: v = 10^((dB-15)/20), dB = 20*log10(v) + 15. Every clip also has a fixed Volume component (match 'Internal Volume Mono' on mono clips) with the same mapping; scripts usually keyframe that one and add this effect only when a second gain stage is needed. The unnamed boolean is very likely Bypass. Effects-panel folder is a best guess.

measured.how: Premiere 26 render, 3 s test signal per setting, analysed with ffmpeg (live wave 3, 2026-10-14)

cards.name: Channel Volume
cards.summary: Sets the level of each channel of a stereo or 5.1 clip separately (for example left and right), in dB.
use_for: Balance a dual-mic interview where one lav channel is louder than the other
Pull down a noisy channel without removing it
Trim one side of a lopsided stereo music or ambience file
avoid: Mono clips: no effect (it does not attach)
To remove a channel completely, Fill Left with Right / Fill Right with Left is cleaner

params.name: Left
params.does: Level of the left channel. Measured: the same scale as clip Volume, 0.1778 = 0 dB (the default), 0 = silent, 0.5 = +9 dB, 1 = +15 dB (dB = 20 log10(v / 0.1778)).

measured.signal: a split stereo pair (L 440 Hz at -12 dBFS, R 1 kHz at -24 dBFS)

params.name: Right
params.does: Level of the right channel. Measured: the same scale as Left (0.1778 = 0 dB, 0.5 = +9 dB, 1 = +15 dB, 0 = silent).

measured.signal: a split stereo pair (L 440 Hz at -12 dBFS, R 1 kHz at -24 dBFS)

cards.scripting: Stereo / multichannel clips only (the mono harvest could not attach it; the batch now holds the stereo dump, match 'Internal Channel Volume'). Properties 'Left' and 'Right' (30 more unnamed rows for channels 3-32), on the clip Volume scale: 0.1778 = 0 dB (default), dB = 20 log10(v / 0.1778), 0 = silent, 0.5 = +9 dB, 1 = +15 dB (measured, live wave 3). Use it to trim or mute one side; stereo clips also carry a fixed Channel Volume component with the same rows.

measured.how: Premiere 26 render, 3 s test signal per setting, analysed with ffmpeg (live wave 3, 2026-10-14)

cards.name: Multiband Compressor
cards.summary: Splits audio into up to four frequency bands (default crossovers about 120 Hz, 2 kHz and 10 kHz) and compresses each separately, with a peak limiter on the output. Tames boomy lows or harsh highs without pumping the whole mix.
use_for: Control boomy proximity-effect lows on a close-miked VO without dulling the voice
Dense broadcast/radio-style narration for news and political explainers
Master the final mix so VO and music are loud but controlled
Tame harsh highs in a music bed under narration
avoid: High ratios on every band squash and pump the mix: sounds over-processed
Defaults barely compress (all thresholds sit at 0 dB): set thresholds or it does almost nothing
Heavier than a single-band compressor; put one instance on the track or mix rather than on every clip

params.name: Threshold 1
params.does: Level above which band 1 (lows, below about 120 Hz) is compressed; inferred dB = -60 + 60*v, default 1 = 0 dB

params.name: Threshold 2
params.does: Threshold for band 2 (about 120 Hz-2 kHz, the body of a voice); inferred dB = -60 + 60*v

params.name: Ratio 2
params.does: Compression ratio for band 2; inferred ratio = 1 + 29*v (default 0.0345 = 2:1)

params.name: Attack 2
params.does: How fast band 2 compression reacts; inferred ms = 500*v (default 0.02 = 10 ms)

params.name: Release 2
params.does: How fast band 2 recovers; inferred ms = 5000*v (default 0.02 = 100 ms)

params.name: Gain 2
params.does: Makeup gain for band 2; 0.5 = 0 dB

params.name: Output Gain
params.does: Overall output gain after the bands; 0.5 = 0 dB. Measured: 0.25 = -9 dB, 0.5 = 0, 0.75 = +9 dB: dB = 36 v - 18 (a +/-18 dB span).

params.name: Cutoff 1
params.does: Crossover between bands 1 and 2; inferred Hz = 20 + 19980*v (default 0.005 = 120 Hz)

cards.scripting: Audition-derived effect; match is a GUID. Every control is normalized 0..1. Unit mappings are inferred from defaults that line up exactly with Audition's (crossovers 120/2000/10000 Hz, 2:1, 10 ms, 100 ms): Threshold dB = -60 + 60v; Ratio = 1 + 29v; Attack ms = 500v; Release ms = 5000v; Cutoff Hz = 20 + 19980v; Gain n / Output Gain 0.5 = 0 dB. Not verified against the panel readout. Bands 1-4 run low to high. Toggles (Bypass n, Solo n, Band n Bypass/Mute, Link band controls, LMAX: Bypass) are 0/1. 'LMAX: ...' rows are the output limiter. Rows from 'Spectrum Show Peak Hold' onward (repeated as #2..#5) and the 'Level Meter ...' rows are analyser/meter UI state: ignore.

measured.how: Premiere 26 render, 3 s test signal per setting, analysed with ffmpeg (live wave 3, 2026-10-14)

cards.name: Notch Filter
cards.summary: Cuts up to six very narrow frequency bands (notches), each with its own frequency, depth and on/off switch, plus DTMF options that remove phone keypad tones.
use_for: Remove 50 Hz mains hum and its harmonics (100, 150, 200 Hz) from Indian field recordings when DeHummer is not enough
Kill a steady whine (camera fan, tube-light buzz, monitor whistle) at a fixed pitch
Remove DTMF keypad tones from a phone-call recording
Notch a feedback ring out of a press-conference PA recording
avoid: Many or wide notches in the voice range make VO hollow and phasey
It only helps on steady-pitch tones; a wrong frequency does nothing useful
Applying it with defaults: all six notches are enabled at preset frequencies and already cut

params.name: Frequency 1
params.does: Centre frequency of notch 1; normalized 0..1, Hz mapping unverified
params.typical: calibrate against the panel, then set to the hum/whine pitch

params.name: Gain 1
params.does: Depth of notch 1; inferred dB = (v - 0.5) * 192 (default 0.3698 = -25 dB)

params.name: Enable 1
params.does: Turns notch 1 on (1) or off (0)
params.typical: 1 for notches in use, 0 for the rest

params.name: Notch Width
params.does: Width selector for all notches. Audition's Notch Filter offers Narrow / Very Narrow / Super Narrow; here it is a normalized 0..1 value (likely 0 / 0.5 / 1, unverified)

params.name: Ultra Quiet
params.does: Lower-noise processing mode (0/1)

params.name: DTMF Lower
params.does: Adds notches for the low DTMF keypad tones (0/1)
params.typical: 1 together with DTMF Upper on phone audio

params.name: DTMF Upper
params.does: Adds notches for the high DTMF keypad tones (0/1)
params.typical: 1 together with DTMF Lower on phone audio

cards.scripting: Audition-derived (GUID match); all controls normalized 0..1. Gains appear to map dB = (v - 0.5) * 192 (defaults decode to -25, -18, -12, -8, -3, -2 dB): inferred, not verified. Frequency mapping is unknown: set Frequency 1 once, read the Hz shown in Effect Controls, and store the mapping before scripting exact pitches. All six notches default to enabled, so set 'Enable n' = 0 for unused ones. 'Fixed Gain' and the DTMF attenuation rows default to 0.65625 (meaning unverified). 'Original Sample Rate' and 'Horizontal Range Start/End' are display rows: ignore. For 50 Hz hum try DeHummer first.

measured.how: Premiere 26 render, 3 s test signal per setting, analysed with ffmpeg (live wave 3, 2026-10-14)

cards.name: Dynamics
cards.summary: All-in-one dynamics processor (the current Audition-derived Dynamics) with AutoGate (silences low-level noise between words), Compressor, Expander and Limiter sections, each switched on separately.
use_for: Even out a talking-head VO with gentle compression
Gate room tone or AC noise between phrases of an interview
Catch peaks with the limiter before export
One-effect VO chain for quick social reels
avoid: AutoGate with a high threshold chops word endings and breaths: sounds choppy
Every section is off by default: applying it alone changes nothing
For precise control prefer Dynamics Processing, Single-band Compressor or Hard Limiter

params.name: Compressor Enabled
params.does: Turns the compressor on (1) or off (0)

params.name: Compressor Threshold
params.does: Level where compression starts; inferred dB = -60 + 60*v (default 0.667 = -20 dB). Measured on a -6 dBFS tone with Compressor Ratio 0.5: 0.25 = -30.1 dB, 0.5 = -18.5, 0.6667 = -10.7 dB of gain reduction, which fits threshold dB = -60 + 60 v with Ratio 0.5 = about 4.3:1 (so not the 1 + 29 v ratio scale of Multiband Compressor).

params.name: Compressor Ratio
params.does: Compression ratio; 0 = 1:1 (none, the default, so enabling the compressor alone does nothing). Measured: 0.5 gives about 4.3:1 (from the gain reduction at three thresholds), so it is NOT the 1 + 29 v scale of Multiband Compressor
params.typical: aim for 2:1-4:1 on VO: somewhere below 0.5 (0.5 = about 4.3:1, measured); the rest of the scale is not measured

params.name: Compressor MakeUp Gain
params.does: Gain added after compression; 0 = 0 dB
params.typical: raise a little until perceived loudness is back

params.name: AutoGate Enabled
params.does: Turns the noise gate on (1) or off (0)

params.name: AutoGate Threshold
params.does: Level below which audio is gated; inferred dB = -60 + 60*v (default -20 dB is too high for most VO)

params.name: Limiter Enabled
params.does: Turns the peak limiter on (1) or off (0)

params.name: Limiter Threshold
params.does: Limiter ceiling; on the inferred -60..0 dB scale the default 0.983 = -1 dB (unverified)

cards.scripting: Audition-derived effect with a GUID match (no legacy Dynamics exists in this install's audio list). All controls are normalized 0..1; the '... Enabled' rows are 0/1 and every section is OFF by default, so set the relevant Enabled row to 1. Unit mappings are inferred from defaults, not verified: threshold rows 0.667 = -20 dB on a -60..0 scale; AutoGate Attack 0.0909 = 1 ms on 0.1..10 ms; AutoGate Hold 0.009 = 10 ms on 1..1000 ms; Compressor/Limiter Release 0.0816 = 50 ms on 10..500 ms. Confirm against the Effect Controls readout before relying on exact dB.

measured.how: Premiere 26 render, 3 s test signal per setting, analysed with ffmpeg (live wave 3, 2026-10-14)

cards.name: Phaser
cards.summary: Sweeping phase-shift filter like the classic guitar pedal: moving notches give a swirling, whooshing, spacey motion to the sound.
use_for: Stylise a riser or whoosh SFX on a trailer transition
Retro or psychedelic treatment on a music sting or flashback
Robotic or sci-fi voice for an AI character (low Mix)
Add movement to a static drone or ambience pad
avoid: On documentary or news VO it sounds like a broken effect
High Feedback with high Intensity turns harsh and resonant

params.name: Mix
params.does: Wet/dry balance (0 = dry, 1 = fully phased). Measured on pink noise: almost no level change (-0.26 dB at 0.5, notches to -1.9 dB): the sweep is heard, not measured, at the defaults.

params.name: Mod Rate
params.does: Speed of the sweep (normalized)
params.typical: 0.02-0.1 for a slow swirl; higher = fast warble

params.name: Depth
params.does: How far the sweep travels (likely 0..1 = 0..100%)

params.name: Intensity
params.does: Strength of the phasing (likely 0..1 = 0..100%)

params.name: Feedback
params.does: Amount of output fed back into the input: further from 0.5 = more resonant, metallic. Audition's range is -100..+100%, so 0.5 is most likely 0% (no feedback) and values below 0.5 feed back inverted
params.typical: 0.5 default; 0.6-0.75 (about +20 to +50%) for a stronger jet sound (scale unverified)

params.name: Stages
params.does: Number of filter stages: more = deeper, more notches

params.name: Upper Freq
params.does: Top of the sweep range; inferred Hz = 20 + 19980*v (default 0.7 = 14 kHz)

params.name: Gain
params.does: Output gain (default 0.75)
params.typical: keep 0.75; lower if the effect makes the clip louder

cards.scripting: Audition-derived (GUID match); all controls normalized 0..1. Mix, Depth and Intensity most likely map 0..1 = 0..100%; the other unit mappings are unverified. Keyframe Mix for swells rather than toggling the effect.
